Formal

FOR-muhl · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Formal is official or extra polite, following the set rules of ceremonies and special occasions; not casual.

The wedding invitation asked everyone to wear formal clothes.

Worked Example

Principal Diaz sent a formal letter to parents, typed and signed.

The letter was typed and signed the proper way, not scribbled like a quick note. Following set rules like that is what formal means.

How Formal Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

proper

proper: the right way to do any task, even small everyday ones; formal is for special occasions and writing with set rules

dressy

dressy: fancy, for special events

Antonyms

casual

casual: relaxed and everyday

informal

informal: not following set rules

How Strong Is It? — Polite → formal → Ceremonial

Polite vs. formal

Polite vs. formal: Polite is milder: saying please and thank you is polite even at a backyard cookout.

Ceremonial vs. formal

Ceremonial vs. formal: Ceremonial is stronger: a ceremonial flag-raising follows exact steps written down long ago.

Put it together

Put it together: Form means shape, so formal describes things that keep the proper, expected shape - like formal clothes or a formal letter.
